### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **36** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/openapi-builtin-paths.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**13** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/discovery (route, a path literal in a comment in registerDiscoveryEndpoints))_
- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/discovery (route, a path literal in a comment in registerDiscoveryEndpoints))_

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via registerDiscoveryEndpoints (symbol, a method of class RestServer; a top-level function), /api/v1/discovery (route, a path literal in a comment in registerDiscoveryEndpoints), /environments/:environmentId (route, a path literal in a comment in registerDiscoveryEndpoints; a path literal in registerDiscoveryEndpoints; a path literal in registerOpenApiEndpoints))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/openapi-builtin-paths.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `enforceAuth (23 routes)`, `resolveExecCtx (28 routes)`, `routeManager (20 routes)`, `resolveProtocol (25 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1 (route, 96 pages)`, `/api/v1/data (route, 40 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6f0e0502015d1a54a2891ce52fad725e1bae17cc` — the merge of head `9ddffc0baad2ca64051703b98f8fc8032d05ebe5` into base `29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6f0e0502015d1a54a2891ce52fad725e1bae17cc && git checkout 6f0e0502015d1a54a2891ce52fad725e1bae17cc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a 9ddffc0baad2ca64051703b98f8fc8032d05ebe5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a && git merge --no-ff 9ddffc0baad2ca64051703b98f8fc8032d05ebe5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `9ddffc0baad2ca64051703b98f8fc8032d05ebe5`
Local-runs: none

**Face:** the declaration face. This is a move-only refactor of `@objectstack/rest`, with one named exception of one token, which the seat has ruled on. The diff does the following:
- two registrar bodies move into one new module;
- one gate's target paths are re-pointed (`scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`);
- one entry is added to a gate's registry (`scripts/adr-anchors/`);
- two platform-checklist source lists and one dogfood matrix row are re-pointed;
- the registrar list that nine readers read grows 7 → 8.

The 17-file list holds no published schema and no governed path. `record-recognisers --template --paths` over it derives `TIER_DEFAULT`, and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded success. Since then, `main` has gained the narrowing face (#23750, `29c7157af4`). This PR's body reads `Clause-②: no` with no arm, and the tree carries no changeset, so that recogniser reads the declaration face too.

**Inputs:**
- card #23050: its body and all 29 comments. These include the triage ruling `6126748916`, slice 1's landing `6136102437`, slice 2's refinement `6189011700`, the slice 6 release `6204146893` (which carried the "two arms" fix to this slice), the claim `6204191684`, the report `6205396354` and the seat's ruling `6205442867`;
- slice 6's record `6203715861` (PR #23729) and slice 5's record `6201318879` (PR #23719), used as precedent;
- PR #23763:
  - its body;
  - its file list (17 files, +933 / −631, matching `git diff --numstat` file for file);
  - the net diff against merge-base `2906cd8d2e`;
  - its one comment (the advisory docs-drift check);
  - its timeline: the labels, and the cross-lane declarations `6205451586` on #6017 and `6205458368` on #6023;
- the 45 check-runs on this head, and the step conclusions of its `Lint ·` and `Type Check` jobs.

The reviewer is an isolated agent working read-only. Every count below was read off the git objects of the merge-base and the head with these tools:
- `git show` and text `diff`;
- `grep`, and a scan of `this.` reads and import bindings with comments and strings stripped;
- the gates' own patterns, applied to text: `check-adr-anchors`' `DECISION_CITATION`, `check-route-envelope`'s two dialect rules, and the dogfood tripwire's two regexes.

Nothing was built, tested or re-run. The merge-base's `rest-server.ts` blob (`4867a14302`) is the same blob as at the dev's base `3b46855fb9`, so the PR's base line numbers apply as written.

### ① Derived judgments

No accept set and no public surface changes. Each change the diff makes is judged below.

1. **The discovery body is byte-identical, and the OpenAPI body differs in exactly one token: right.**
   - Base `rest-server.ts` `:4914`–`:5235`, with one 4-space indent removed, equals head `discovery-routes.ts` `:123`–`:444`. That is 322 lines, and 0 differ.
   - Base `:5324`–`:5590`, de-indented the same way, against head `:454`–`:720` (267 lines): exactly one line differs.
     - It is base `:5525` / head `:655`: `RestServer.overlayDocumentationInfo(` became `this.overlayDocumentationInfo(`.
     - The rest of that line is equal.
   - The only unindented lines in either range are the `/docs` viewer's template-literal continuation (base `:5564`–`:5574`). They are runtime HTML at column 0, and they moved byte for byte.
   - The other odd-backtick lines in the ranges (four in discovery, two in OpenAPI) are line comments. So no other template literal spans the cut, and removing the indent changes no runtime string.
   - Both private methods keep their name, docblock and position. The call sites in `registerForBase` (head `:4791`–`:4796`) are unchanged, so the four routes register in the same order on every base.
   - The rest of the `rest-server.ts` side is:
     - the two stubs (a host literal plus `.call`);
     - the new import and its comment;
     - three import-pointer comments;
     - the re-worded `DISCOVERY_ROUTE_KEY_TO_SERVICE_SLOTS` docblock.
   - Its top-level `export` lines are identical at base and head. The file goes from 10,636 to 10,090 lines.

2. **Each host lists exactly what its body reads: right.**
   - **The discovery body's `this.` reads** (comments and strings excluded):
     - `config` 9 and `routeManager` 2;
     - `resolveProtocol`, `probeMcpServeable`, `getDirectMountRouteBases` and `getMountedEmailRouteBase`, 1 each.
     - `DiscoveryRouteHost` declares exactly those 6.
   - **The OpenAPI body's reads:**
     - `config` 1, `routeManager` 2, `resolveExecCtx` 2 and `enforceAuth` 2;
     - `loadOpenApiSpec`, `getRoutes`, `resolveProtocol`, `resolveEndpointMatchAuthority` and `notifyMissingEndpointAuthority`, 1 each;
     - after the one token, `overlayDocumentationInfo` 1.
     - `OpenApiRouteHost` declares exactly those 10.
   - **The discovery body reads no `this.protocol`.**
     - The name appears only in the `[#9292]` comment (`discovery-routes.ts` `:128`, `:151`).
     - The body reaches the protocol through `resolveProtocol`.
     - So the dev's finding that hypothesis (a) is partly falsified is right.
   - Neither body has a bare `this`, an element access on `this`, or a `function` token.
   - Each host is an object literal of its interface, typed by indexed access on the class, so a missing or an extra member is a compile error. `TypeScript Type Check` and the four `Type Check ·` lanes concluded success.

3. **Value or getter, member by member: right.**
   - **`routeManager` goes by value in both literals.**
     - All four `register` calls are top-level statements of the bodies, so they run during registration.
     - The class reassigns the field only at head `:5175` / `:5179`, the try/finally around `registerMetadataEndpointsInner`. `registerRoutes` calls these registrars outside it.
     - Each literal is built when its stub runs. So the two tests that call `registerOpenApiEndpoints` directly read the field exactly as base did.
   - **`config` goes as a getter in both literals.**
     - Each of the ten reads is inside a handler, so each happens at request time: `discoveryHandler` spans `:124`–`:423` and holds its nine reads at `:204`–`:413`; `openApiHandler` holds its one read at `:655`.
     - The field is not `readonly` (`:2021`), and only the constructor assigns it (`:2166`). A by-value copy would not follow a later reassignment; the getter would.
     - The getter reads through a closure over the server (`readConfig`), never through the host. This is slice 2's refinement, applied field by field.
     - The dev's by-value ablations are theirs, not re-run here. They match this reading.
   - **Methods** go as late-bound closures that call the method on the server. So the receiver of every helper is still the server, and a spy set after registration is still reached.

4. **Ruling A on the private static is right. This review would have ruled the same.**
   - **The receiver change cannot alter an answer.**
     - The static (head `:4964`) reads no `this` and no `arguments`. Its only inputs are its two parameters, and it returns `bundled` or a new object.
     - The host member is a closure that calls `RestServer.overlayDocumentationInfo` with the same arguments, and it reads that member at call time. So the receiver (`RestServer`), the late binding and the arguments are the base call's.
     - The one runtime difference is one more stack frame.
   - **B is refused, rightly.** A module-level binding named `RestServer` would keep the bytes, but it names something that is not the class.
   - **C is worse.** Moving the static out of the class removes a `private static` line from the published `.d.ts`. If it also left `rest-server.ts`, it would strand the ten `packages/spec/liveness/rest_api.json` rows anchored at `rest-server.ts#overlayDocumentationInfo`, which this slice may not edit. A keeps all ten exact.
   - **A fourth shape, not among the options, is worse too:** an element access, `RestServer['overlayDocumentationInfo'](…)`, on a value import of the class.
     - It also changes the token.
     - It defeats `private` on purpose.
     - It bypasses the named host that the card's ask 2 requires.
   - A is the only shape that both:
     - changes one token and nothing that is published;
     - reaches the class member through the one named context object the card asks for.
   - The card's contract holds. Each handler's logic is unchanged, and the route table is unchanged.

5. **The imports moved as a pure move: right.**
   - The bodies read these module-level bindings of base `rest-server.ts`:
     - seven imports: `isMcpServerEnabled` (`@objectstack/types`), `enrichOpenApiWithEndpoints`, `buildBuiltinPaths`, `selectServedEndpoints`, `sendThrownError`, `handleRouteError` and `logError`;
     - two of the file's own declarations: `DISCOVERY_ROUTE_KEY_TO_SERVICE_SLOTS` and the type `RestProtocol`.
   - The module imports each from the same specifier.
   - The first five imports have no code use left in `rest-server.ts`, so they left it. Each left an accurate pointer comment.
   - `handleRouteError` and `logError` still have code uses there, so they stay.
   - `DISCOVERY_ROUTE_KEY_TO_SERVICE_SLOTS` and `RestProtocol` were already exported (base `:884` and `:257`). No export was added.
   - The value import makes the two modules import each other. `data-action-routes.ts`, `batch-routes.ts`, `approvals-routes.ts` and `analytics-routes.ts` already do the same.
     - The table is read only inside the handler, so no evaluation order can see it uninitialised.
     - `RestServer` is imported as a type only.

6. **The published surface is unchanged: right.**
   - `@objectstack/rest` publishes `dist` only. tsup builds it from the single entry `src/index.ts`, with `splitting: false`, and emits the `.d.ts` from that entry.
   - `src/index.ts` is untouched. It re-exports from `./rest-server.js` by name only, and it names neither the new module nor `DISCOVERY_ROUTE_KEY_TO_SERVICE_SLOTS`.
   - The host interfaces appear only inside private method bodies, which declaration emit does not reach.
   - The private methods' docblocks and the `private static` member are unchanged. The one docblock this diff re-words in `rest-server.ts` sits on a const that no exported declaration reaches.
   - The dev's `.d.ts` sha and export-list readings are theirs, not re-run here. They are what this construction predicts. The bundle's JS bytes change; its behaviour does not.

7. **`scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` was re-pointed, not loosened. Its comments state the counts right.**
   - By the gate's own rule on the module:
     - `stringError` is 0: no `error` key has a string initializer;
     - `siblingCode` is 0: no body has `code` beside `error` at its top level.
   - The answers each handler builds:
     - the one hand-built refusal is the nested `{ error: { code: 'OPENAPI_UNAVAILABLE', message } }` (`:478`–`:479`);
     - the discovery handler's catch is `handleRouteError`;
     - the two OpenAPI catch-alls are `sendThrownError`.
   - So `rest-server.ts` stays at 17 / 17, and both sums hold:
     - `stringError`: 17 + 13 + 8 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 39;
     - `siblingCode`: 17 + 15 + 8 + 9 + 4 + 1 + 0 + 0 = 54.
   - The table grows from 17 to 18 rows, with 8 → 9 ratcheted. The new row is `dialectOnly` with ratchet `#9559`, like the six moved modules before it.
   - **The slice 6 fix is right.** The `siblingCode` entries above it record four arms: #7981's two `handleError` arms (77 → 75) and #8073's two 500 arms (75 → 73). This closes slice 6's non-blocking item and the release's carry.
   - The `Response-envelope guard` step concluded success in `Lint · docs & code guards`.

8. **The new ADR anchor is right, needed and in proportion. Omitting ADR-0057 is right.**
   - **Why it is needed:**
     - `DECISION_CITATION` finds 5 citations in the module: ADR-0057 D10, ADR-0076 D12 ×2, ADR-0056 D2 and ADR-0138 D2. That is exactly the 3 + 2 in the two moved ranges.
     - `rest-server.ts` goes from 94 to 89.
     - The letter layer reads every citation in every anchored file (`check-adr-anchors.mjs` `:930`). Without this entry, those five would leave its reading while the gate stayed green. That is the dead-pin shape the card forbids.
   - **The listed ids:** each appears in the module, and each cited letter is a decision of its record:
     - ADR-0076 `### D12`: honest capabilities;
     - ADR-0056 `### D2`: anonymous default-deny;
     - ADR-0138 `### D2`: the closed list of doors.
   - **The invariant adds no citation.** It writes "its D12" and "its D2", so the gate's pattern finds 0 in it.
   - **Its attributions match the records and the moved code's own comments.** The OpenAPI single-owner clause rests on the code's "(#5078, ADR-0076)". #5078 frames a second `/openapi.json` owner as ADR-0076's shadow-duplication class, so the attribution holds.
   - **ADR-0057** is one of the three numbers in `KNOWN_NUMBER_COLLISIONS` (two records share it). Leaving it out narrows nothing, and listing it would add a fourth entry to the ambiguous-number note:
     - the letter layer reads and resolves `ADR-0057 D10` whatever the list says;
     - the base anchor for `rest-server.ts` lists only ADR-0045, so the id layer never held this citation at base either.
   - Note, not a defect: the invariant says each handler's first act refuses an anonymous caller.
     - In fact the identity read (`resolveExecCtx`) comes first, because the refusal needs it.
     - The moved `[#22430]` comment and the matrix row use the same wording.
     - The invariant's closing clause states the property exactly: a door that answers before the anonymous refusal is the drift.
   - It is a registry entry of an existing gate, not a new gate. The `ADR anchors + number uniqueness` step concluded success in `Lint · repo & tooling gates`.

9. **The registrar list and its readers were re-counted exactly. Nothing was loosened.** The list grows 7 → 8 by an appended entry. Each reader was recounted at head over the eight files:
   - **execctx census:**
     - `resolveExecCtx` mentions go 109 → 113 (57 + 12 + 7 + 9 + 12 + 3 + 9 + 4).
     - `rest-server.ts` stays at 57: two sites moved out, and one forwarder's two mentions came in.
     - The module holds the two sites and one interface member's two mentions.
     - Forwarder lines in `rest-server.ts` go 8 → 9.
   - **`MOVED_REGISTRARS_READING_NO_EXECCTX` is an exact re-count, not a tolerance.**
     - The forwarder count is pinned at exactly (8 − 1) + 3 − 1 = 9, and both maps' sums are pinned exactly, at 3 and 1.
     - A respelt or dropped forwarder reads 8 and reds.
     - A discovery body that starts reading the seam gains a forwarder, reads 10 and reds.
     - The alternative, a `resolveExecCtx` forwarder on a host whose body never reads it, would break the rule in item 2.
     - Like `EXTRA_MOVED_REGISTRARS`, the map's keys are summed, not located. All forwarders live in `rest-server.ts`, so a line count could not locate them either. The control is exactly as strong as before.
   - **dogfood blind-spot row:**
     - `this.routeManager.register(` is 63 = 23 + 9 + 5 + 7 + 8 + 1 + 6 + 4: `rest-server.ts` went 27 → 23, and the module holds 4.
     - `private register*Endpoints(` is 16, `registerPerItemRoute(` 8 and `const registerPerItemRoute =` 1, each unchanged. The population 70 / 19 / 51 is unchanged.
     - **`enforceAuth` goes 92 → 96** = 41 + 11 + 7 + 9 + 12 + 3 + 9 + 4.
       - `rest-server.ts` stays at 41: two call sites out, the forwarder's two mentions in.
       - The module holds the two sites and the interface member's two mentions.
       - No call site was added. The control is re-anchored on the same population with the seam counted, as slices 4–6 did.
     - The new control `discovery-routes.ts: this.routeManager.register(` reads 4, and the list length 8.
   - **ui-view pair:** `this.enforceAuth(` goes 55 → 56 and `this.resolveExecCtx(` 70 → 71, one forwarder each. The ownership guard stays at 1, and the floors of 40 are unchanged.
   - **docblock pin:**
     - The module holds exactly 5 TSDoc blocks (the header, two interfaces, two functions), and its floor is 5.
     - The moved ranges held 0, so `rest-server.ts` stays at 164 against its floor of 100.
     - The floors' sum goes 29 → 34: the new module's actual 5 added to an unchanged 29. The sum is pinned.
   - **query-number 9, canonical-query 4, meta-draft 8:** the module has 0 numeric coercions, 0 `query:` literals and 0 draft tokens. Each floor is 0, and each sum is unchanged.
   - **dogfood realtime tripwire:** both probe regexes read 0 over all eight files.
   - All nine importers of `rest-server-registrar-files.ts` are in the diff.

10. **The other re-points are pure re-points: right.**
    - **`api-backend.json`:** in the `crud_endpoints` and `metadata_endpoints` source lists, the `(registerDiscoveryEndpoints — …)` clause leaves the `rest-server.ts#` entry.
      - It returns as `+ packages/rest/src/discovery-routes.ts#registerDiscoveryEndpoints (…)`, with its explanatory text unchanged. That is slice 2's form (`:2261`).
      - The new anchor names an exported function at that path.
      - `check:platform-checklist` is kept out of per-PR CI by design (`lint.yml`). The dev's local reading (735 / 745 resolved, unresolved 10 → 10) is theirs.
    - **The matrix row `anonymous-deny-api-description`:** only `rest/rest-server.ts` → `rest/discovery-routes.ts` changes. The enforcement it describes is the moved body's, unchanged.
    - **Prose:** the two `openapi-builtin-paths.ts` docblocks and the `DISCOVERY_ROUTE_KEY_TO_SERVICE_SLOTS` docblock are comment-only edits, accurate about where the caller now lives.
    - Note: the re-worded `buildBuiltinPaths` sentence still says the handler hands it "`routeManager.getAll()`". Since #5822 the handler has passed `this.getRoutes()` (`discovery-routes.ts` `:513`). The dev names this stale fact as pre-existing. It is not a contract defect.
    - **Other whole-file readers of `rest-server.ts` that are not on the list read no moved line:**
      - `auth-gate-allowlist-fault-window` reads the auth-gate block;
      - `execctx-authz-input-seam-reachability` reads `computeExecCtx`;
